new_entities.name: Betaine HCl supplementation
new_entities.description: Oral betaine hydrochloride used with the goal of transiently re-acidifying the stomach in people with hypochlorhydria or acid-suppressed gastric conditions.

new_entities.name: Hypochlorhydria symptoms
new_entities.description: Symptoms or functional consequences associated with low stomach acid, including impaired gastric acidification and related upper gastrointestinal complaints.

edges.effect_quant: In the cleanest mechanistic human study, 1500 mg betaine HCl lowered mean gastric pH from 5.2 to 0.6 and kept pH below 3 for about 73 minutes in rabeprazole-induced hypochlorhydria. Drug-absorption crossover trials confirm that this re-acidification can be pharmacologically meaningful, but the same literature also shows the effect is context-dependent and not the same thing as proven symptom relief.
edges.population: healthy volunteers with pharmacologically induced hypochlorhydria or acid-suppressed gastric conditions
edges.mechanism: Betaine HCl acts as an exogenous acid donor that can transiently restore gastric acidity, potentially reversing the impaired dissolution and upstream digestive environment caused by suppressed stomach acid.
edges.summary: Betaine HCl clearly re-acidifies the stomach for a short window, but the leap from that pharmacologic effect to routine symptom relief is much less proven. The evidence supports a real mechanistic action with mixed clinical implications rather than a broadly validated low-stomach-acid remedy.
edges.caveats: Most studies were done in healthy volunteers with induced hypochlorhydria and evaluated pH or drug absorption rather than patient-reported digestive symptoms. The benefit may differ substantially in fed versus fasted states.

evidence.notes: Gastric reacidification with betaine HCl in healthy volunteers with rabeprazole-induced hypochlorhydria.

effect_quant.comparator: mean gastric pH change after 1500 mg betaine HCl

evidence.notes: The use of betaine HCl to enhance dasatinib absorption in healthy volunteers with rabeprazole-induced hypochlorhydria.

effect_quant.comparator: AUC restored relative to dasatinib alone after rabeprazole pretreatment

evidence.notes: Meal Effects Confound Attempts to Counteract Rabeprazole-Induced Hypochlorhydria Decreases in Atazanavir Absorption.
